items.followUp: How does unequal sharing of electrons create partial charges in a polar covalent bond?

rubric.why: A polar covalent bond is formed by unequal sharing of the bonding electron pair.
rubric.description: Unequal sharing of the electron pair
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the bonded atoms share the electron pair unequally, due to a difference in electronegativity.

rubric.why: Unequal sharing creates partial positive and partial negative ends.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that unequal sharing produces partial positive and partial negative ends (poles).

modelAnswer: A polar covalent bond forms when bonded atoms share the electron pair unequally because of a difference in electronegativity.
This unequal sharing produces partial positive and partial negative ends in the bond.
